newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican development bank Nafin says restructured.
newsitem.headline: Mexican development bank Nafin says restructured.

text.p: Mexican development bank Nacional Financiera (Nafin) said on Sunday it restructured its divisions to better control risk and provide credit to small and medium-sized businesses.

"The restructuring is...a redistribution of administrative areas and positions with the aim of making more dynamic and functional the completion of the 1997 Financing Program," the bank said in a statement.
Changes include a new Risk Administration department, which will evaluate liability and asset risks, and will control the bank's exposure, Nafin said.
A new Adjunct Investment Projects department will place capital for larger industrial companies and assume some of the risk for the credits, Nafin said.
The bank said it will also focus on boosting credit for small and medium-sized companies.
Earlier this month Nafin sold 1.5 billion pesos of bank development bonds and officials say it will issue $600 million public and private placements in the second half of the year.
